rationale:
Split into two independent children. Each is a genuine obligation from a different area, and neither is in the pinned Mathlib or SimonGMT. The parent keeps only its step 1 (the a.e. modification) and the final bookkeeping.

(1) covector_finite_dimensional. The supplied proof asserts without proof that Λ = Covector (Euclid P) n is finite-dimensional, and uses this to get a countable basis. In the Submission scope, Mathlib has no FiniteDimensional, SecondCountableTopology, ProperSpace or MeasurableSpace instance on continuous alternating maps (checked with #synth / fail_if_success). This is linear algebra, not measure theory, and the same fact is needed elsewhere. Two other branches reserve the identical type: dor_ims_sua_covector_finiteDimensional (decomposing) and imsupp_covector_finiteDimensional (still 'comparing'). Neither was comparator-accepted at decision time, so this child gets a globally unique name. Whichever is accepted first can close the others by `exact`.

(2) lusin_measurable. This is Lusin's theorem in compact form for Borel-measurable maps from ℝ^P into any second-countable space: arbitrary μ, a measurable A with μ A ≠ ∞, and ε : ℝ≥0∞ with ε ≠ 0. It is exactly steps 2–5 of the supplied proof, generalized only to the target properties those steps use. Mathlib has only Lusin–Souslin and Lusin separation.

Parent assembly (the supplied proof):
- By (1), FiniteDimensional.proper_real and secondCountable_of_proper, Λ is second countable; `borelize` Λ.
- Step 1: f' := hf.mk f is measurable. Take a measurable null set Z ⊇ {f ≠ f'} (exists_measurable_superset_of_null) and put A₀ := A ∖ Z.
- Apply (2) with Y = Λ, g = f', the set A₀ and ENNReal.ofReal ε ≠ 0. This gives a compact K ⊆ A₀ ⊆ A with μ(A₀∖K) < ofReal ε on which f' is continuous.
- Then μ(A∖K) ≤ μ(A₀∖K) + μ(Z) < ofReal ε, and f = f' on K gives ContinuousOn f K.

subproblems.title: Covectors on ℝ^P form a finite-dimensional real vector space
subproblems.statement: For all natural numbers P and n, the real vector space Covector (Euclid P) n = Λⁿ(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional over ℝ. This is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the "Notation" paragraph of the parent proof. It asserts that Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n is a finite-dimensional real normed space and uses this only to get a countable basis of open sets of Λ. The pinned Mathlib has no FiniteDimensional instance for continuous alternating maps, so the fact is proved here.
Notation: E := ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). Λ := Covector E n = E [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on E, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication. For I : Fin n → Fin P, e ∘ I denotes the n-tuple (e_{I(i)})_{i ∈ Fin n}.
1. (Basis.) Let e = (e_i)_{i ∈ Fin P} be the standard basis of E: EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, viewed as a Module.Basis (Fin P) ℝ E via .toBasis.
2. (Evaluation map.) Define L : Λ → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) by L(α)(I) := α(e ∘ I) for every index map I : Fin n → Fin P. For fixed I, the map α ↦ α(e ∘ I) is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because (α + β)(v) = α(v) + β(v) and (c·α)(v) = c·α(v). Hence L is ℝ-linear.
3. (Injectivity.) Let α, β ∈ Λ with L(α) = L(β). Then α(e ∘ v) = β(e ∘ v) for every v : Fin n → Fin P, in particular for every injective v.
 An alternating n-linear map on a module with basis e is determined by its values on the tuples e ∘ v with v injective (Module.Basis.ext_alternating). [Directly: write each argument as x_j = Σ_i x_j^i e_i and expand by multilinearity. This gives α(x) = Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_{j ∈ Fin n} x_j^{I(j)}) α(e ∘ I), so α is determined by the numbers α(e ∘ I).]
 Hence the underlying alternating maps of α and β coincide. A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective), so α = β. Thus L is injective.
4. (Conclusion.) The codomain (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ is a finite-dimensional real vector space, because the index type Fin n → Fin P is finite (it has P^n elements). A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective, applied to L and step 3). Therefore Covector (Euclid P) n is finite-dimensional over ℝ for all P and n. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix the standard basis e of ℝ^P: (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis.
L(α) := (α(e ∘ I))_{I : Fin n → Fin P} is an ℝ-linear map from Covector (Euclid P) n to (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ.
L is injective: Module.Basis.ext_alternating identifies the underlying alternating maps, and ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective identifies the continuous ones.
(Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ is finite-dimensional, so FiniteDimensional.of_injective L gives FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n).

subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem (compact form) for measurable maps from ℝ^P into a second-countable space
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, and let Y be a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. Let μ be any measure on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) (Borel σ-algebra), let A ⊆ ℝ^P be a measurable set with μ(A) < ∞, let g : ℝ^P → Y be measurable, and let ε ∈ (0, ∞] be an extended nonnegative real with ε ≠ 0. Then there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε such that g is continuous on K (ContinuousOn g K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Y) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), Measurable g → MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ε ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn g K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–5 of the parent proof, which is the standard proof of Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17) in the compact form used by the parent. Here they are applied directly to a measurable map g, so the parent's measurable-modification step 1 is not needed (take A₀ = A). The target Λ is replaced by an arbitrary second-countable space Y, because steps 2–5 use only a countable basis of the target and the measurability of preimages of open sets. The error budget ε·2^{−k−2} is replaced by summable positive weights η_k, which also covers ε = ∞.
Hypotheses: P ∈ ℕ. Y is a second-countable topological space with a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. μ is any measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra). A ⊆ ℝ^P is measurable with μ(A) < ∞. g : ℝ^P → Y is measurable. ε ∈ [0, ∞] with ε ≠ 0.
1. (Inner regularity inside A.) Let ν := μ.restrict A, so ν(B) = μ(B ∩ A) for measurable B.
 ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(A) < ∞. A finite measure is locally finite, and ℝ^P is a σ-compact (indeed proper) metric space, so ν is regular (Mathlib instance Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Hence ν is inner regular by compact sets on measurable sets of finite measure (InnerRegularCompactLTTop). (Alternatively, Ulam's theorem: finite Borel measures on the Polish space ℝ^P are tight.)
 Consequently (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt), for every measurable B ⊆ A and every η ∈ (0, ∞] there is a compact C ⊆ B with ν(B ∖ C) < η. C is compact in a Hausdorff space, hence closed and measurable. So B ∖ C is measurable and contained in A, and ν(B ∖ C) = μ((B ∖ C) ∩ A) = μ(B ∖ C). Thus μ(B ∖ C) < η.
2. (Countable basis.) Since Y is second countable, fix a countable basis 𝓑 of its topology. Y is nonempty (it contains g(0)) and ⋃𝓑 = Y, so 𝓑 is nonempty. Enumerate it as 𝓑 = {O_k : k ∈ ℕ}, with repetitions allowed. Each O_k is open, hence measurable in Y. Since g is measurable, S_k := g^{−1}(O_k) is a measurable subset of ℝ^P.
3. (Weights.) Choose η_k ∈ (0, ∞) for k ∈ ℕ with Σ_k η_k < ε. For example, put δ := min(ε, 1) ∈ (0, 1] and η_k := δ·2^{−k−2}; then Σ_k η_k = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε. (In Mathlib: ENNReal.exists_pos_sum_of_countable'.)
4. (Compact pieces.) Fix k. The sets A ∩ S_k and A ∖ S_k are measurable subsets of A. By step 1 with η = η_k/2 > 0, choose compact sets C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with
 μ((A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) < η_k/2 and μ((A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k) < η_k/2.
 Put E_k := C_k ∪ D_k, a compact subset of A. Let x ∈ A ∖ E_k. If g(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ (A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k; otherwise x ∈ (A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k. Hence A ∖ E_k ⊆ ((A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) ∪ ((A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k), and subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k/2 + η_k/2 = η_k.
5. (The compact set.) Let K := ⋂_k E_k.
 Each E_k is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, so K is closed. K lies in the compact set E_0, so K is compact, being a closed subset of a compact set. Also K ⊆ E_0 ⊆ A.
 Since A ∖ K = ⋃_k (A ∖ E_k), countable subadditivity and steps 3–4 give μ(A ∖ K) ≤ Σ_k μ(A ∖ E_k) ≤ Σ_k η_k < ε.
6. (Continuity.) Fix k and x ∈ K, so x ∈ E_k = C_k ∪ D_k.
 - If x ∉ D_k, then x ∈ C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k, so g(x) ∈ O_k.
 - If g(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ S_k, so x ∉ D_k because D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k.
 Hence K ∩ g^{−1}(O_k) = K ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ D_k). D_k is compact, hence closed, so ℝ^P ∖ D_k is open. Therefore the preimage of O_k under the restriction g|_K : K → Y is open in the subspace topology of K.
 Every open subset of Y is a union of sets O_k, so its preimage under g|_K is a union of open subsets of K, hence open (IsTopologicalBasis.continuous_iff). Therefore g|_K is continuous, i.e. ContinuousOn g K (continuousOn_iff_continuous_restrict).
 Together with step 5, K is a compact subset of A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε on which g is continuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν = μ.restrict A is finite, so it is regular on ℝ^P (a σ-compact metric space) and hence InnerRegularCompactLTTop. So each measurable B ⊆ A contains a compact C with μ(B ∖ C) = ν(B ∖ C) < η.
Enumerate a countable basis (O_k)_{k∈ℕ} of Y; it is nonempty because g(0) ∈ Y. Each S_k = g⁻¹(O_k) is measurable.
Choose positive weights η_k with Σ η_k < ε, e.g. min(ε,1)·2^{−k−2}.
Choose compact C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with defects < η_k/2. Then E_k = C_k ∪ D_k ⊆ A has μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k.
K = ⋂_k E_k is closed inside the compact E_0, hence compact. K ⊆ A and μ(A ∖ K) ≤ Σ_k μ(A ∖ E_k) < ε.
For x ∈ K, g(x) ∈ O_k ⇔ x ∉ D_k. So (g|_K)⁻¹(O_k) = K ∩ D_kᶜ is open in K, and by the basis criterion g is continuous on K.
